headline: Samsung could overtake SK Hynix as the world's biggest supplier of high-bandwidth memory in 2027, Digitimes reports, citing forecasts from an industry forum in Seoul.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the article itself could not be read, so the forecast's source, size and assumptions are unverified, and the forum was on 6 Oct 2026.
importance_line: If the forecast holds, the leading supplier of the fast memory that AI chips depend on would change from SK Hynix to Samsung, but it is a forecast and its source and assumptions are not known.
summary: Digitimes reports that Samsung Electronics could pass SK Hynix as the largest supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the fast memory stacked beside AI chips, in 2027 as HBM4 prices climb and makers compete for limited DRAM production capacity, according to forecasts presented at an industry forum in Seoul on 6 Oct 2026.
notes: Digitimes is behind a subscription; the summary restates the headline and the publisher's preview only. Forum date 6 Oct 2026 is before the cut-off, so the QA re-dated check may hold it. Not previously carried in our editions.
